# Datagrid — Technical Reference Complete reference for `@filemark/datagrid` + its integration into `@filemark/mdx`. Intended as the source-of-truth for column type semantics, info-string grammar, persistence keys, and the adapter contracts the datagrid assumes from its host. - Package: `@filemark/datagrid` (`packages/datagrid/`) - Integration: `@filemark/mdx` (`packages/mdx-viewer/src/DataBlock.tsx` + `remark-code-meta.ts`) - Showcase example: `examples/datagrid-full.md` --- ## 1. Goals - **Interactive table from markdown.** Any `.md` author can promote a block of tabular data to a sortable / filterable / resizable grid by using a fenced ` ```csv ` (or ` ```tsv` / ` ```datagrid `) code block. - **Rich column types.** Beyond string / number / date / bool, a single info-string flag upgrades a column to a status badge, avatar, progress bar, currency, clickable URL, tag set, etc. - **Portable.** Zero host-platform imports. Works unchanged in the Chrome extension, a future VS Code webview, or a plain web demo. - **Persistent where it matters.** Sort / filter / column widths / column visibility survive reloads. Interactive checkbox cells persist per-row when an `id` column exists. --- ## 2. Authoring model Three gateways, all pre-existing markdown surfaces — no new MDX / JSX required: | Syntax | Purpose | |---|---| | ` ```csv ` | Inline CSV, comma-separated by default | | ` ```tsv ` | Inline TSV, tab-separated | | ` ```datagrid ` | Alias when the delimiter is set explicitly in `` | Example: ````md ```csv type:priority=status(P0:danger,P1:warn) sort=priority title="Tickets" id,title,priority t-01,Fix mailer,P0 t-02,Polish docs,P1 ``` ```` No JSX component is involved. The underlying pipeline (see §5) intercepts these code fences and replaces them with a ``. This keeps the author-facing surface ordinary markdown that renders static in any other viewer (GitHub, VS Code preview) — the interactive layer degrades gracefully to a plain code block. ### `src=` — external CSV file Leave the body empty and set `src=./some.csv`. The viewer's `AssetResolver` resolves the relative path → URL, then `fetch`-es it: ````md ```csv src=./data/sales.csv type:revenue=currency(USD) ``` ```` Works when the file was opened via **Open Folder** (FSA handle) or drag-dropped as a whole folder. Single-file drops do not have sibling access; the block renders a human error instead of silently showing no rows (Rule 3 — skeleton honesty). ### `` — component-style tag The lowercase `` (or capitalized `` — HTML parsers lowercase element names either way) is registered in the `react-markdown` components map and behaves exactly like a fenced block with `src=`, but reads more naturally inline: ```md ``` Supported attributes (mirror the info-string flags): | Attribute | Maps to | |---|---| | `src` | `src=` | | `title` | `title=` | | `sort` | `sort=` | | `filter` / `search` | `filter=` / `search=` | | `height` | `height=` (px) | | `hide` | `hide=` (comma-sep) | | `delimiter` | `delimiter=` | | `id-column` / `idColumn` | `id-column=` | | `row-numbers` / `rowNumbers` | `row-numbers=` | | `meta` | raw info-string — carries `type:=…` / `align:=…` flags that HTML attribute names can't hold (a colon isn't clean in an HTML attribute-name position) | **Important — always use a closing tag (``), never self-closing (``).** HTML5 self-closing syntax only applies to void elements (`
`, ``, etc.). For any other custom element the browser's HTML parser *ignores* the trailing `/>` and treats it as an open tag, so *all subsequent markdown becomes children of the tag* — swallowing the rest of the document. This is a parser-level behavior, not something we can override. Always close explicitly. **Inline data is not supported in the tag.** HTML attributes can't hold multi-line CSV cleanly (escaping newlines, commas, ampersands becomes untenable). If you have inline data, use a ` ```csv ` fenced block. **Missing `src=`** → renders an amber warning card, not an empty grid. --- ## 3. Info-string grammar After the lang tag on a fence, the remainder is the info-string. The parser is a shell-ish k=v splitter (whitespace-separated, quotes respected, parens group internal whitespace): ``` ::= | no- | = | type:= | align:=left|right|center ``` - Bare `` → true. `no-` or `=false` → false. - `` may be quoted (`"`, `'`) to include spaces. - `type:=` installs a rich renderer on that column. - Unknown flags log a warning to the browser console; the block still renders with defaults for anything that couldn't be parsed. ### Global flags | Flag | Default | Notes | |---|---|---| | `filter` / `no-filter` | on | show per-column filter row | | `search` / `no-search` | on | global search input in toolbar | | `sort=[:asc\|desc]` | — | initial sort; comma-separated for multi-sort (`sort=a:asc,b:desc`); `sort=false` disables sorting UI | | `hide=,,…` | — | pre-hide listed columns | | `delimiter=` | `,` (csv) / `\t` (tsv) | override parsing delimiter; use `\\t` literally for tab | | `header` / `no-header` | on | if off, columns become `col_0`, `col_1`, … | | `src=` | — | load CSV via `AssetResolver.resolve(path)` or absolute URL via direct fetch | | `height=` | 420 | px height of the scroll region | | `title=` | "data" | toolbar label + export filename stem | | `sticky-header` | on | header stays visible on vertical scroll | | `row-numbers` | off | prepend a `#` column (1-based, always pinned) | | `id-column=` | — | marks row-id column (alias for `type:=id`) | | `type:=` | — | see §4 | | `align:=` | inferred | force alignment | | `width:=` | auto-size | override the initial width of a column (positive number). User can still drag / double-click to change; new width is persisted. | | `agg:=` | — | aggregation footer; `` is `sum\|avg\|min\|max\|count\|uniq`. Recomputes on filter changes; formatting follows the column type. When `group-by=` is also set, the same aggregation functions render inside each group-header row | | `freeze=,,…` | — | left-pin listed columns during horizontal scroll | | `density=` | `comfy` | initial row-density preset (also toggleable in toolbar, persisted) | | `selection` | off | show checkbox selection column; enables bulk **Copy CSV / MD / JSON** toolbar buttons when rows are selected | | `group-by=` | — | group rows by that column; group headers collapse / expand and show per-group aggregations | | `expandable` | off | prepend a chevron column; clicking it reveals a vertical "detail panel" with every column's value for that row | | `url-sync` | off | mirror grid state (sort / filters / hide / density / group / expand / search) into `location.hash#g=…` so shared links reproduce the view | --- ## 4. Column types ### 4.1 Primitives (inferred from sample rows, no hint required) | Type | Recognized when… | |---|---| | `string` | fallback | | `number` | every sampled cell parses as a finite number | | `date` | every sampled cell is a `Date.parse`-able string of length ≥ 4 | | `bool` | every sampled cell matches `true/false/yes/no` case-insensitively | Alignment defaults: - `number`, `currency`, `percentage`, `filesize` → `right` - `bool`, `checkmark`, `checkbox`, `rating`, `color` → `center` - everything else → `left` ### 4.2 Rich types All require an explicit `type:=` hint. | Type expr | Synopsis | |---|---| | `status` | colored pill, convention-driven (done/pending/failed/…) | | `status(k1:tone,k2:tone,…)` | explicit value→tone map | | `tags` | comma-split pills with deterministic per-tag color | | `tags()` | custom separator (e.g. `tags(\|)`) | | `checkmark` | read-only ✓ / — indicator | | `checkbox` | interactive toggle, persisted when an `id` column is present | | `rating` | 5 stars by default | | `rating()` | ``-star max | | `progress` | inline bar, 0..100 default | | `progress(:)` | custom numeric scale | | `currency` | default `USD` formatting | | `currency()` | force currency code (`EUR`, `JPY`, …) | | `percentage` | auto-scales 0..1 values ×100; 1..N kept as-is | | `filesize` | bytes → KB/MB/GB/TB/PB | | `url` | clickable link, shows `hostname + path` | | `email` | `mailto:` link | | `phone` | `tel:` link | | `code` | monospace inline, muted background | | `color` | swatch + hex; accepts `#RGB`/`#RRGGBB`/`#RRGGBBAA` | | `date` | localized `Apr 23, 2026` | | `relative` | `5m ago` / `in 3d`; hover for absolute | | `avatar` | initials circle + label; cell `Name\|https://img.png` → image | | `sparkline` / `sparkline(line\|bar\|area)` | comma-separated numbers → inline 64×16 SVG chart (line, bar, or filled area) | | `icon` | named icon from a curated 15-icon set (`check`, `x`, `warning`, `info`, `star`, `heart`, `lock`, `rocket`, `bug`, `clock`, `flame`, `bolt`, `shield`, `mail`, `link`); unknown → raw text | | `country` | ISO-2 code → flag emoji + code; non-ISO → text | | `duration` / `duration(s\|ms\|m\|h)` | numeric → `1d 2h 3m` formatted (max two parts); default input unit `s` | | `range` / `range()` | `start..end` (or custom separator) → auto-detects date / numeric → `Jan 5, 2026 → Feb 12, 2026` / `100 – 200` | | `code-block` | multi-line monospace (max-height 192 px, internal scroll) | | `json` | parses + pretty-prints in monospace; invalid JSON rendered red | | `image` | absolute URL → 32×32 thumbnail linking to full image in new tab; relative paths await AssetResolver threading (v2.1) | | `id` | monospace uuid, click-to-copy, marks the row-id column | ### 4.3 Color tones (shared by `status`) Tone → Tailwind classes (sympathetic to light / dark themes): | Tone | Classes | |---|---| | `success` | `bg-emerald-500/15 text-emerald-700 dark:text-emerald-300 border-emerald-500/30` | | `warn` | `bg-amber-500/15 text-amber-700 dark:text-amber-300 border-amber-500/30` | | `danger` | `bg-red-500/15 text-red-700 dark:text-red-300 border-red-500/30` | | `info` | `bg-blue-500/15 text-blue-700 dark:text-blue-300 border-blue-500/30` | | `muted` | `bg-muted text-muted-foreground border-border/60` | | `primary` | `bg-primary/15 text-primary border-primary/30` | | `secondary` | `bg-secondary text-secondary-foreground border-border/60` | Aliases accepted in color maps: `green→success`, `red→danger`, `amber/yellow/orange→warn`, `blue→info`, `gray/grey/neutral→muted`. Convention defaults (`status` without explicit map): | Cell value (lowercased) | Tone | |---|---| | `done`, `ok`, `complete(d)`, `success`, `pass(ed)`, `active`, `yes`, `live` | `success` | | `pending`, `todo`, `wip`, `in-progress`, `review`, `waiting`, `draft` | `warn` | | `fail(ed)`, `error`, `blocked`, `cancel(l)ed`, `rejected`, `no`, `expired` | `danger` | | `info`, `note`, `new` | `info` | | anything else | `muted` | ### 4.4 Deterministic color hashing `tags` and `avatar` (initials mode) derive a palette index from the value via FNV-1a. Same input → same color across files / sessions / machines. Tag and avatar palettes are separate (8 tones each). --- ## 5. Pipeline ``` react-markdown ├─ remarkPlugins: [remarkGfm, remarkMath, remarkBreaks, remarkCodeMeta] │ └─ remarkCodeMeta copies node.meta (the info-string) onto │ hast data-meta so the `code` component can read it. │ └─ components.code (in MDXViewer) lang ∈ {mermaid,schema,prisma,dbml,csv,tsv,datagrid} ── csv/tsv/datagrid branch ──→ ├─ parseInfoString(meta) → DataGridOptions ├─ opts.src ? assets.resolve(src).fetch().text() │ : codeBlockChildren └─ ├─ parseCSV({ text, delimiter, typeSpecs, … }) │ Papaparse → inferTypes → type-coerce cells → { columns, rows } └─ ├─ TanStack Table (sort, filter, column visibility, sizing) ├─ TanStack Virtual (row virtualization) ├─ CellRenderer (dispatch on Column.type → cells.tsx) └─ StorageAdapter persistence (sort/filter/sizes/visibility + per-cell checkbox) ``` Why `react-markdown` and not `@mdx-js/mdx`: MV3's strict CSP bans `unsafe-eval`, which `@mdx-js/mdx`'s evaluation path requires. The datagrid path uses plain code fences, so no eval is involved. --- ## 6. Persistence `StorageAdapter` is injected via `ViewerProps.storage`. The datagrid reads/writes two kinds of keys: ### 6.1 Grid state (per block) `filemark:datagrid:` → ```json { "sorting": [{"id":"priority","desc":false}], "columnFilters": [{"id":"owner","value":"Ada"}], "columnVisibility": {"internal_id": false}, "columnSizing": {"title": 280, "owner": 180} } ``` Debounced (250 ms) on change after initial hydration. `storageKey` is assembled in `DataBlock`: ``` :: ``` so a block's state sticks to that *specific* block — re-ordering blocks in the file re-keys them, which is the intended behavior (restart fresh when the document meaningfully changes). ### 6.2 Interactive cell state (per row × col) `filemark:datagrid::cell::` → boolean Only used by `type: "checkbox"`. `rowId` is resolved by reading the value of the column designated via `type:=id` (or `id-column=`). If no id column is set, `CheckboxCell` still renders interactively but doesn't persist — the `` title explains the situation. --- ## 7. `AssetResolver` integration ```ts export interface AssetResolver { resolve(relativePath: string): Promise; } ``` Implementations live in `apps/chrome-ext/src/app/adapters/`: | Host context | Implementation | `resolve()` returns | |---|---|---| | FSA folder (`kind: "fsa"`) | `FSAAssetResolver` | `blob:` URL from `FileSystemFileHandle.getFile()` | | Drop-folder (`kind: "drop"`) | `DropAssetResolver` | `blob:` URL from in-memory `Map` | | `file://` intercept | passthrough `new URL(rel, sourceUrl)` | works for ``, **not** for CSV fetch | | Remote (raw.github etc.) | passthrough | works when host permission covers the origin | Datagrid-specific `src=` flow (lives in `DataBlock.tsx`): 1. `src` starts with `http://` / `https://` / `file://` / `blob:` / `data:` → skip `AssetResolver` entirely, `fetch(src)` directly. Works from any ingest context (single-file drop, folder, intercepted file://). 2. Relative `src` + `AssetResolver` present → `assets.resolve(src)`. - Null returned → error card: `path not found: `. 3. Relative `src` + no `AssetResolver` → error card: "relative paths require a folder-opened context. Open via a folder picker, use an absolute https:// URL, or inline the data." 4. On success → `fetch(url).then(r => r.text())` → Papaparse → DataGrid. 5. `TypeError: Failed to fetch` from step 4 → surfaced as "likely CORS, a bad URL, or no network — check DevTools Network for the exact reason". ### CORS — current state and plan **Current (v0.1 — Option A):** `manifest.json` declares `host_permissions: [""]`. Chrome treats every `fetch()` from an extension page as privileged for those origins, so CORS headers on the target server no longer matter — arbitrary public CSV URLs load transparently. Cost of this choice: the Chrome Web Store install prompt now reads "Read and change your data on all websites". For a doc viewer this is broad. We accepted it for v0.1 because there's no CORS-bypass mechanism in MV3 that doesn't require some flavor of host permission. Filemark only *fetches* data from those hosts; it never injects scripts, writes, or exfiltrates. **Planned (Option B — later):** switch to `optional_host_permissions` + on-demand grants. Install prompt goes back to just `"storage"`; the first time the user loads `https://foo.example/data.csv`, the datagrid error card surfaces a "Grant access to foo.example" button. One click → `chrome.permissions.request({origins: ["https://foo.example/*"]})` → retry. Permission is persistent per-origin once granted. Work items for Option B (scoped): 1. Manifest: `host_permissions` → `optional_host_permissions`. 2. New `PermissionAdapter { hasHostAccess(origin), requestHostAccess(origin) }` interface in `@filemark/core`. 3. `ChromePermissionsAdapter` in `apps/chrome-ext/src/app/adapters/` wrapping `chrome.permissions.contains` + `chrome.permissions.request`. 4. Thread the adapter through `ViewerProps` alongside `storage` + `assets`. 5. `DataBlock.tsx`: on `TypeError: Failed to fetch`, if a permission adapter is present and doesn't yet hold access for the target origin, render a Grant button that calls `requestHostAccess` and re-triggers the fetch on resolution. Tracked as the follow-up to M7 in `TASKS.md`. Estimated ~40 lines across 5 files. ### Path safety Resolvers must refuse paths that escape the root (`../../..`). FSA gets this for free (directory-handle walk); passthrough resolvers should `new URL()`-normalize. --- ## 8. Exports Toolbar exposes two download buttons: - **JSON** — current *visible* rows (post-sort, post-filter) projected through currently-visible columns. Written as `{title}.json`. - **MD** — same projection as a GFM table; alignment hint preserved in the separator row (`:---:` / `---:` / `---`); pipes / backslashes / newlines escaped in cell text. Written as `{title}.md`. Both use `URL.createObjectURL(blob)` + a programmatic `` + a short `setTimeout` revocation. --- ## 9. Styling The datagrid ships no CSS file of its own. All visual style is Tailwind utility classes co-located on JSX, aligned to shadcn tokens (`bg-card`, `text-foreground`, `border-border`, `bg-primary`, …) so themes adapt automatically. **Host Tailwind must scan workspace packages.** Tailwind v4's automatic source detection only scans the current app's source. Workspace packages must be opted in explicitly: ```css /* apps/chrome-ext/src/styles/index.css */ @import "tailwindcss"; @source "../../../../packages/*/src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}"; ``` Without this directive, classes the datagrid introduces (but that the host doesn't itself use) — `cursor-col-resize`, compound hovers, etc. — silently drop from the final CSS. --- ## 10. Layout — CSS grid + TanStack Virtual - **CSS Grid** drives both the header row and every body row. A single `gridTemplateColumns` string is computed from `header.getSize()` on each render. Columns *always* align vertically because every row shares the identical template. - **TanStack Virtual** positions rows absolutely with `translateY`. `measureElement` is bound via ref so that rows whose content wraps (long cells, markdown) re-measure after first paint and adjust the total scroll height. - **Horizontal scroll.** The inner wrapper's `width` is set to the sum of current column widths, so the outer `overflow-auto` container scrolls when columns overflow. Header and body share the container, so horizontal scroll syncs automatically. - **Sticky header.** `sticky top-0` on the header grid row (works because its parent is `overflow-auto`). --- ## 11. Column resize - `enableColumnResizing: true` + `columnResizeMode: "onChange"` on the TanStack table. - Each header renders a 1px right-edge separator (`bg-border`) that widens to 3px + `bg-primary/70` on hover, full `bg-primary` while dragging. - `onMouseDown` / `onTouchStart` bound to `header.getResizeHandler()`. - `onDoubleClick` → `header.column.resetSize()` restores the auto-computed default. - Sizes persist in the grid-state blob (§6.1). ## 11a. Multi-column sort - `enableMultiSort: true` + `enableMultiRemove: true` on the TanStack table. - Click a header → replaces the current sort. Shift-click a header → appends a secondary sort (or removes it if the same column is shift-clicked three times). - Active sort ordinals (`1`, `2`, `3`) render next to the sort indicator when more than one sort is live. - Initial multi-sort comes from the info-string's comma-separated `sort=a:asc,b:desc` form. ## 11b. Row selection + bulk copy - `selection` flag enables row selection. A checkbox column is prepended on the far left (always pinned). - TanStack's `enableRowSelection: true`, `onRowSelectionChange`, and a `getRowId` derived from the `idColumn` (falls back to row index) drive the state. - When any rows are selected, the toolbar shows three buttons: **Copy CSV / Copy MD / Copy JSON**. They project the selected rows through the currently-visible columns and write to `navigator.clipboard`. - Header checkbox toggles the entire *currently-filtered* row model (not the raw dataset) and shows an indeterminate state when the selection is partial. ## 11c. Aggregation footer - `agg:=` installs a per-column aggregation where `` is `sum | avg | min | max | count | uniq`. - The footer row sits sticky at the bottom of the scroll region (`position: sticky; bottom: 0`) so it always stays visible. - Computed over `table.getRowModel().rows` (i.e. the currently filtered / sorted view), so numbers update live as filters change. - Formatting respects the column type via `formatAgg()`: - `currency` columns → locale-aware currency string with the column's `args.currencyCode` (defaults to `USD`). - `percentage` → auto-scales 0..1 values, formats with `%`. - `filesize` → auto K/M/G/T units. - `count` / `uniq` → plain integer regardless of column type. - Everything else → `toLocaleString` with 2 fraction digits. ## 11d. Density - Three presets: `compact` (26 px row height, `py-0.5`), `comfy` (34 px, `py-1.5`), `relaxed` (44 px, `py-2.5`). Font size scales too (12/13/14 px). - Seed via the info-string (`density=compact`) or cycle at runtime via the toolbar button (**Compact → Comfy → Relaxed**). The choice is persisted via `StorageAdapter` as part of the grid-state blob. ## 11e. Match highlight - Any filter or search term causes matching substrings inside plain-text / markdown cells to be wrapped in `` with an amber background. Respects both the global search and per-column filters (the union of terms is highlighted). - Lives inside `renderInlineMd()` in `cells.tsx`. Multiple terms build a case-insensitive regex; the walker splits text fragments by that regex before emitting. - Structured cell types (`status`, `tags`, `avatar`, `currency`, etc.) don't highlight — their content isn't free text and the match UI would be noisy. ## 11f. Pinned (frozen) columns - `freeze=,,…` pins the listed user columns to the left. The `_select` and `_rowno` meta columns are *always* pinned. - Implemented with CSS grid + `position: sticky; left: ` on each pinned cell. Cumulative left offsets are computed from the current column sizes so pins stack correctly and respond to resizing. - Z-index layering: pinned header cells use z-20, pinned body cells z-10, so they always sit above non-pinned content during horizontal scroll. A faint right-edge shadow visually separates the pinned region from the scrolling region. ## 11h. Row grouping (v1.2) - Single-column grouping via `group-by=`. TanStack's `getGroupedRowModel` + `enableGrouping: true` + a `GroupingState` of `[col]` does the heavy lifting. - Group header rows render with a chevron, the group value, and a count; indentation grows with `row.depth × 12 px` (we currently only ship single-level grouping, but the renderer supports any depth). - Per-column `aggregationFn` is wired from the `agg:=` info-string flag (`sum → sum`, `avg → mean`, `count → count`, `uniq → uniqueCount`, `min → min`, `max → max`). The group header's aggregated cells render via the column's `aggregatedCell` and format the value using the column type (currency stays currency, filesize re-units, etc.). - Group expansion state is part of the grid-state blob and survives reload. ## 11i. Row expansion / detail panel (v1.2) - `expandable` flag + `getRowCanExpand: () => true` + TanStack's expanded-row model. Prepends a chevron column (`_expand`) that toggles the expanded state per row. - When expanded, a `` renders beneath the row: a `display: grid` two-column definition list iterating the user's visible columns, each value rendered through the same `CellRenderer`. Great for the wide-table problem — reading a row without horizontal scrolling. - Virtualization handles variable heights automatically — the outer absolute-positioned wrapper contains both the row and the optional panel; `rowVirtualizer.measureElement` measures the combined height. ## 11j. Typed filter UIs (v1.2) - Each column's type maps to a `FilterFamily`: - numeric (`number`, `currency`, `percentage`, `progress`, `filesize`, `rating`) → `number-range` — two `` min / max. - `date` / `relative` → `date-range` — two `` from / to. - `status` / `tags` → `multi-select` — dropdown with colored chips sourced from the distinct values in the dataset. - `bool` / `checkmark` / `checkbox` → `bool-tristate` — one button that cycles `any → ✓ yes → ✗ no → any`. - everything else → `text` — the previous substring filter. - `filterFn` on each column picks the matching predicate; TanStack's filter state holds whatever shape the family uses (string, tuple, array, boolean, or null). - Match highlight (§11e) remains but only pulls a highlight term from `string`-family filters — highlighting substrings that leaked from a numeric range would be noisy. ## 11k. URL-sync (v1.2) - `url-sync` opts the grid into serializing sort / filters / visibility / density / grouping / expanded / global-search state into `location.hash`. - Format: a base64-URL-encoded JSON object keyed under a single `g=` fragment. Other hash fragments (heading anchors) are preserved. - On mount we read the URL state *after* the StorageAdapter state, so a shared link overrides the local preference — makes reproducing a view from a URL reliable. - Writes use `history.replaceState` (no history entries spammed) and are debounced 250 ms with the adapter write. - Only the grid's own state is serialized; column *sizes* stay per-machine via the StorageAdapter (different viewport widths need different column widths). ## 11g. Keyboard navigation - The scroll container is `tabIndex={0}` + `role="grid"` and owns a keyboard handler. Typing targets inside the grid (filter / search inputs) are excluded from the hotkeys. - Supported keys: | Key | Action | |---|---| | `↑` / `↓` | move focused row | | `←` / `→` | move focused column | | `Home` / `End` | first / last column in the row (`⌘/Ctrl+Home/End` for first / last row) | | `PageUp` / `PageDown` | ±10 rows | | `/` | focus the search input | | `Space` | toggle selection on the focused row (when `selection` is on) | - Focused row gets a subtle `ring-ring/60` inset ring; focused cell gets a thin outline. `rowVirtualizer.scrollToIndex(focusedRow)` keeps the focused row in view. - Screen-reader wiring (`aria-rowcount`, `aria-colcount`, `aria-selected`, `role="gridcell"`, `role="row"`) is present but full grid-keyboard a11y (tabindex roving, selection announcement) is a v2 item — see §14. --- ## 12. Auto-size heuristic On first render, each column's default width = `clamp(80, longestContentChars × 7.5 + 32, 480)` — sampled across the header label and the first 30 rows (truncated to the first line for each cell). Hits ~95% of "reasonable" CSV-ish data without user intervention; user-resize is always the final word and is persisted. --- ## 13. Public API (TypeScript) ```ts // From @filemark/datagrid export function DataGrid(props: DataGridProps): JSX.Element; export function DataGridFromText(props: DataGridFromTextProps): JSX.Element; export function parseCSV(input: ParseCSVInput): DataGridTable; export function parseInfoString(meta: string | undefined): DataGridOptions; export function parseColumnType(expr: string): ColumnTypeSpec | null; export function inferTypes(seeds, rows, hints?): Column[]; export interface Column { key: string; label: string; type: ColumnType; align?: "left" | "right" | "center"; hidden?: boolean; args?: ColumnTypeArgs; } export type ColumnType = | "string" | "number" | "date" | "bool" | "status" | "tags" | "checkmark" | "checkbox" | "rating" | "progress" | "currency" | "percentage" | "filesize" | "url" | "email" | "phone" | "code" | "color" | "relative" | "avatar" | "id"; ``` See `packages/datagrid/src/types.ts` for the full shape. --- ## 14. Limitations (v1) - No column grouping / multi-row headers. - No pivot tables (aggregation footer ships in v1.1; group-by is queued). - Cell editing limited to the `checkbox` type — this is a reader app, not an editor. - `src=` only fetches CSV; it does not stream. 5 MB+ files parse synchronously on the main thread. A worker-based streaming path is a v2 item. - Sparkline / icon / country / json / duration types are designed but deferred (v2 batch). - No ARIA `role="grid"` yet — the table uses `
`s for virtualization; a11y is "works with VoiceOver, not great" — proper grid roles + keyboard nav is a v2 task. --- ## 15. Extension points Adding a new rich type takes four touches: 1. Append the literal to the `ColumnType` union in `types.ts`. 2. Add the name (and any arg shape) to `parseColumnType.ts` → `TYPE_NAMES` + `parseArgs`. 3. Export a new `` from `cells.tsx`. 4. Add the dispatch branch in `CellRenderer.tsx`. If the type needs numeric sort / right-align, also extend the `isNumeric` / `defaultAlign` helpers in `DataGrid.tsx` and `parseCSV.ts`. --- ## 16.
